rv.q: Now the City Lit Theater in Chicago has reincarnated “Shane” into an extraordinary and psychologically riveting stage play, and it compares favorably to the film.
City Lit's new season is off a strong start with this production.
As the haunted, sad-eyed hero, Woods gives one of the best performances I’ve seen on a Chicago stage this year.
It's a gripping story; not for nothing has it been adapted multiple times... Pracht pulls it off for the most part, finding nuance in unexpected places and shading his characters beautifully.
As the titular mysterious drifter, Michael B. Woods is outstanding, conveying from the beginning Shane's constant struggle against his past as a killer.
The strong performances, impressive fight choreography, and detailed worldbuilding make the story engaging from beginning to end.
City Lit’s Shane is earnest, capable entry for anyone looking to step into the Wild West for an evening.

Pracht has taken some excellent material and has now included some exciting nuances that have brought something unique to the story, especially with respect to the lead role of Shane, captivatingly played by Michael B. Woods.
Together, the rustic set and detailed projections create a fully realized Wyoming landscape.
But this is not to say that any of the characters are well-developed- instead, they are conspicuously wooden, one-dimensional.

cn.t: Critics praise this world premiere Western adaptation for its exploration of positive masculinity and Michael B. Woods' captivating lead performance, though the stage setting can't match the novel's wide-open vistas.
